## Madrid Tenant Notice: Preparation Checklist

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

You’re best served by organizing the notice, the lease history, and any proof of how the apartment has been used. The goal is to be ready for a landlord discussion, mediation, or legal review without assuming the notice is automatically valid.

## What to Ask, Gather, and Compare

| Topic | What to ask | What to gather | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|---|
| Notice details | When exactly was notice delivered? Was it in writing? Does it cite a specific legal basis and date to vacate? | Notice letter, envelope/email, delivery proof, screenshots, WhatsApp messages | Timing and formal delivery often matter in disputes |
| Lease history | What was the original term? What changed at renewal? Was the renewal written or automatic? | Signed lease, renewal addendum, payment history, prior notices | Lease type and renewal terms can affect rights and deadlines |
| Personal-use claim | Who will use the apartment, for what purpose, and when? Is the stated reason consistent? | Any landlord statements, messages, ads, property listings, witness notes | A personal-use reason is often tested against consistency and evidence |
| Apartment status | Is it furnished? What furniture/inventory was included? Any separate deposit or inventory list? | Inventory list, photos at move-in/out, deposit receipt, condition report | Furnished status can affect damage, return, and handover issues |
| Rent and payments | Are all rents paid on time? Any arrears, partial payments, or disputed charges? | Bank transfers, receipts, rent ledger, utility bills if relevant | Payment history can strengthen your position in negotiations |
| Communications | What has been said before the notice? Were there repair complaints or disputes? | Email chain, messages, repair requests, maintenance tickets | Prior conflict can explain motive or negotiation leverage |
| Timeline | What happened before the notice, and what deadlines are coming next? | Simple chronology with dates | A clean timeline helps a lawyer or adviser assess the case quickly |

## Preparation Checklist for a Tenant in Spain

- Save the notice exactly as received, including headers, attachments, and timestamps.
- Build a one-page timeline:
  - Lease start: 2025-02-01
  - Renewal date: the date of the renewal you signed or accepted
  - Notice date: the day it was delivered
  - Claimed move-out date: 2026-03-01
- Collect the full lease package:
  - Original signed lease
  - Renewal document or written confirmation
  - Inventory/furnished list
  - Deposit terms
  - Any annexes or house rules
- Gather payment proof:
  - Bank transfers
  - Rent receipts
  - Deposit receipt
  - Utility payments if they are part of the dispute
- Save all communications:
  - Email threads
  - WhatsApp chats
  - Text messages
  - Voice notes, if they mention the reason for termination
- Take dated photos:
  - Current condition of the apartment
  - Furniture and appliances
  - Any damage or maintenance issues
- Keep a contact log:
  - Landlord name
  - Agent or administrator name
  - Phone numbers and email addresses

## Negotiation Points That May Be Worth Raising

- Ask for the landlord’s explanation in writing, with the intended personal use described clearly.
- Request more time if you need it to find housing, especially if you have children, work constraints, or limited market availability.
- Propose a mutually agreed handover date in exchange for a smoother exit and a clean inspection.
- Ask about return of deposit and final utility settlement before move-out.
- If the apartment is furnished, confirm in writing what must stay and what condition is expected at handover.
- If there were repairs or unresolved issues, ask whether they can be settled before departure.
- If you suspect a different motive, keep the tone neutral and ask for supporting details rather than making accusations.

## What Usually Matters in a Spanish Tenant Dispute

| Factor | Often important | Less important by itself |
|---|---|---|
| Written notice | Clear wording, delivery proof, deadline | Verbal statements alone |
| Lease wording | Term, renewal clause, termination language | Informal side comments |
| Reason for ending | Specific, consistent personal-use explanation | General dissatisfaction without proof |
| Tenant performance | Rent paid, no major breach, good records | Minor disagreements without documentation |
| Landlord conduct | Consistent messages and follow-through | One-off remarks |
| Evidence quality | Dates, signatures, screenshots, receipts | Memory alone |
| Handover issues | Deposit, inventory, condition report | Unverified claims |
| Timeline | Whether deadlines were met | Confusing or incomplete chronology |

- Spanish housing law overview: https://www.boe.es/legislacion/codigos/codigo.php?id=178
- Madrid tenant support and housing guidance: https://www.madrid.es/
- General citizen advice in Spain: https://administracion.gob.es/
